findings.title: Distribution test does not verify per-process assignment
findings.body: The test `test_flusher_processes_limit` asserts only that the total number of shards assigned across all processes equals 4 (`total_shards = sum(len(shards) for shards in flusher.process_to_shards_map.values()) == 4`). This passes even if the modulo distribution is broken — for example, all four shards could be assigned to a single process, or a shard could be duplicated across processes — as long as the total counts to 4. The test never submits spans, so it does not exercise the actual per-process flushing of shared shards either. There should be explicit assertions like `assert flusher.process_to_shards_map == {0: [0, 2], 1: [1, 3]}` and a round-trip test that submits spans on each partition and verifies they get flushed.

findings.title: Vestigial time.sleep suggests flaky timing dependency
findings.body: `test_basic` now calls `time.sleep(0.1)` between `step.poll()` and `step.join()` with the comment "Give flusher threads time to process after drift change". Since the test already does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at the top of the function, this sleep is a no-op (it just invokes the patched lambda) and provides no actual scheduling guarantee. This is a code smell indicating that the test depends on wall-clock timing that is no longer being controlled. If the test was flaky without this sleep, the root cause should be fixed by polling for the expected condition instead of sleeping.

findings.title: Dead method _create_process_for_shard
findings.body: The method `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is defined but never called anywhere in the codebase. The restart path in `_ensure_processes_alive` always uses `_create_process_for_shards` to bring back the whole process (and therefore all shards mapped to it). Either delete the dead method, or use it as a true per-shard restart hook so that one bad shard doesn't take down its siblings sharing the same process.

findings.title: Dead-branch check `if not process`
findings.body: Inside `_ensure_processes_alive` the loop guards with `if not process: continue`. `self.processes` is a `dict[int, SpawnProcess | Thread]` and is only ever assigned live objects in `_create_process_for_shards`, so this guard can never be true and serves no purpose. The subsequent `if not process.is_alive():` already covers dead processes, so this line should be removed to avoid misleading readers.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag names for the same flusher
findings.body: The same flusher uses two different tag keys for the shard identifier: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` at line 185 but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` at line 199. Existing dashboards that key off one of these tag names will silently break or split when the producer switches to multiprocess mode. Pick one key ("shard" since `flusher_unhealthy` already uses that) and use it consistently.

findings.title: Off-by-one in MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS allows one extra restart
findings.body: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the check `if self.process_restarts[process_index] > MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` happens *before* `self.process_restarts[process_index] += 1`. With `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS = 10`, the sequence is 0,1,...,10 (pass), 11 (fail). That means the consumer tolerates 11 restarts of a given process before giving up, not 10 as the constant name suggests. Either increment before the check or use `>=` so the documented limit matches behavior.

findings.title: max_processes=0 silently becomes 'one process per shard'
findings.body: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `0` the same as `None` because `0 or X` evaluates to `X`. A caller that explicitly passes `0` (e.g., a test, or a future config switch) gets the opposite of what they asked for. Use `if max_processes is not None else len(...)` so `0` is honored as "no flusher processes".
